R6.note: Clean spacing, clear offers and a coherent blue illustration system make this easy to use, though the visual identity feels more digital than tactile.

B8.note: Warm editorial typography, earthy colors and pottery illustrations give the studio a convincing identity while keeping both offers understandable.

defects: The large circular illustration comes before the headline on mobile, pushing the explanation and primary actions down the page.
H2.note: Strong typography and clear course details work well, but the abstract hero graphic is less immediately expressive of a small pottery studio.

C7.note: A clear proposition, distinctive vessel illustration and strongly differentiated offer cards produce a polished, easy-to-follow landing page.

defects: A large, nearly empty band beneath the desktop hero buttons separates the introduction from the offers.
The mobile navigation is very small and crowded.
U4.note: The essential offer is understandable, but default-looking typography, plain cards and an empty hero treatment feel like a competent generic template.

defects: The brand name and top-right call to action wrap awkwardly across multiple lines in the mobile header.
The desktop contact form occupies a narrow left column with a large unused area to its right.
C6.note: The restrained green palette and bold vessel graphic establish a direction, but awkward mobile header wrapping and uneven composition weaken the execution.

H7.note: Consistent blue accents, a recognizable pottery illustration and well-organized offer sections make this a credible and responsive studio page.

defects: The desktop contact section leaves a large unused area beside the narrow form.
The mobile header navigation is very small.
Y2.note: Warm colors and straightforward offer cards communicate the brief, but the generic centered hero and conventional styling provide little studio-specific character.

Z2.note: The oversized headline and blue vessel create a confident identity, with clear prices and course structure, although the heavy typography feels less relaxed.

defects: Desktop supporting copy and navigation are noticeably small relative to the surrounding space.
X5.note: A straightforward warm-toned layout presents the offers clearly and stacks sensibly on mobile, but lacks a distinctive visual connection to the studio.

Z4.note: Elegant serif typography, a terracotta vessel and concise offer cards form the most cohesive expression of a small, unhurried pottery studio.

K9.note: Expressive typography, an unmistakable pottery graphic and highly legible offer cards deliver a strong hierarchy that translates especially well to mobile.
